description: A finished, self-contained 2D Earth-orbit transfer workbench. Users edit circular departure and arrival altitudes, rehearse a Hohmann transfer, inspect signed burns and live telemetry, and skip insertion to see why a second burn is needed. Restrained paper-and-deep-teal instrument styling, true-scale canvas visualization, timeline controls, presets, pan/zoom, and an in-product model guide.

numericalAssumptions: Earth gravitational parameter μ = 398600.4418 km³/s² and equatorial radius = 6378.137 km.
Massless spacecraft under point-mass Earth gravity; all trajectories are planar and prograde.
Circular departure and arrival orbits; instantaneous tangential impulses; a single Hohmann half-ellipse joins the two radii.
Analytic ellipse propagation solves Kepler's equation. Units are kilometers, seconds, and kilometers per second.
Elliptic Kepler solver uses normalized mean anomaly, Newton iteration with a bracketed bisection fallback, and a nominal residual threshold 2e-14 radians.
Altitude input domain is 160–50000 km. All Earth and orbit distances share one scale; spacecraft, maneuver markers, and velocity-vector length are illustrative.
Elapsed time zero is just after burn 1. At the exact arrival time the enabled burn 2 has already been applied. Omitting burn 2 leaves the spacecraft on the transfer ellipse.
Normal rehearsal horizon is transfer time plus one quarter arrival orbital period. With insertion disabled, the horizon is a full transfer orbital period.
Playback clamps a frame gap to 0.1 wall-clock seconds and pauses when hidden, avoiding large jumps when inactive.
limitations: No atmosphere, drag, Earth oblateness, finite-duration thrust, plane changes, perturbing bodies, collision avoidance, navigation errors, or rendezvous targeting.
GEO preset means a circular orbit at the approximate altitude 35786 km, without longitude or inclination modeling.
Hohmann transfers are not globally minimum-Δv for all large radius ratios; bi-elliptic transfers are outside scope.
Abstract Earth markings are not a geographic map.
Educational workbench, not flight operations software.
